2019_131_031919regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of March 19, 2019 at the Services Building. Its principal action authorizes the 2019 School Building and Site Bonds in an amount not to exceed $27,000,000 — the third series drawn on the $125,000,000 bond proposal Troy voters approved November 5, 2013. It also awards $822,140.00 of districtwide site work to Asphalt Specialists, Inc. and $288,420.00 of asbestos abatement to Trust Thermal Abatement, carries the January 2019 Treasurer's Report with total disbursements in period of $10,412,414.95, and amends the 2018-19 budget across ten ancillary funds.
2019_131_031919regmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting, March 19, 2019, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**Recognition**
The Mission Moment honors a Prudential Spirit of Community Award recipient, and the Board recognizes Wass Elementary School as a State School of Character.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the February 5 workshop and February 26 meeting, the January 2019 Treasurer's Report, and an ancillary funds budget amendment.

**Treasurer's Report — January 2019**
General Fund check disbursements total $4,980,973.78 and total disbursements in period are $10,412,414.95. At January 31, 2019 the General Fund balance stands at $22,442,908, consolidated Debt Service at $11,713,241 and consolidated Special Revenue at $2,630,135.

**The 2018-19 budget amendment**
The resolution amends the general appropriations and budget for fiscal 2018-19 across ten funds, each a first amendment: Food Service, Troy Career Center, Adult Education and Community Service, Troy School District Preschool, Facilities Rental, Capital Maintenance, the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, the 2016 Capital Projects Fund, the Early Childhood Learning Center Capital Projects Fund and the Sinking Fund Capital Projects Fund. The Food Service Fund is amended to $4,244,139. The packet notes the resolution need not be read in its entirety but must be made part of the official minutes.

**8.C — the third bond series**
The $125,000,000 bond issue was approved by voters on November 5, 2013, and the district now proceeds with the third series, not to exceed $27,000,000, designated the "2019 School Building and Site Bonds" (unlimited tax general obligation). Dr. Richard Machesky and Rick West are the individuals authorized to accept a purchase offer on the bonds. The attached authorizing resolution recites that the 2013 proposal permitted issuance in one or more series for remodeling, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and re-furnishing school buildings and other facilities to enhance security; acquiring and installing technology equipment and infrastructure; constructing additions; preparing, developing and improving sites; and purchasing school buses — and that under Section 6 and Section 16 of Article IX of the Michigan Constitution of 1963, the tax levies for those bonds are without limitation as to rate or amount.

**Remaining business**
Districtwide site work projects are awarded to Asphalt Specialists, Inc. at $822,140.00 from the Building and Site Sinking Fund, with a bid tabulation attached. Asbestos abatement is awarded to Trust Thermal Abatement at $288,420.00, supported by a bid tabulation and a NOVA Environmental contractor award recommendation listing bids by building. Cabling infrastructure for the Troy School District Preschool is awarded to Complete Interactive Technologies at $59,905.31, and aquatic sports timing equipment for Athens rounds out the business items. A personnel item covers elementary and secondary appointments.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, March 19, 2019, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition — A. TSD Mission Moment: Prudential Spirit of Community Award, B. State School of Character – Wass Elementary School; 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda — A. Minutes of the February 5, 2019 workshop, B. Minutes of the February 26, 2019 meeting, C. Treasurer's Report – January 2019, D. Ancillary Funds Budget Amendment; 6. Personnel — A. Consideration: Elementary and Secondary; 7. Curriculum; 8. Business — A. Districtwide Site Work Projects, B. Districtwide Asbestos Abatement, C. 2019 School Building and Site Bonds, D. Troy Preschool Technology Cabling Bid Update, E. Aquatic Sports Timing Equipment for Athens; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other; 11. Adjournment. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition.** Two items open the meeting: a TSD Mission Moment recognizing a Prudential Spirit of Community Award recipient, and recognition of Wass Elementary School as a State School of Character.

**Treasurer's Report, January 2019.** Rick West transmits the check register including current period voids, together with listings of ACH debits, wire transfers and P-Card purchases, certifying that the disbursements were payments made for obligations of the Troy School District and that all materials or services listed on the invoices have been received or performed. General Fund check disbursements total $4,980,973.78, and total disbursements in period are $10,412,414.95. The summary revenue and expense budget reports for the period ending January 31, 2019 give a General Fund balance of $22,442,908, a consolidated Debt Service Funds balance of $11,713,241 and a consolidated Special Revenue Funds balance of $2,630,135. The bulk of the packet's middle sections is the January check register itself, run by fund.

**Consent item: 2018-19 budget amendment resolution.** The attached Budget Amendment Resolution for the 2018-19 fiscal year covers ten funds, each receiving its first amendment of the year: the Food Service Fund, the Troy Career Center Fund, the Adult Education and Community Service Fund, the Troy School District Preschool Fund, the Facilities Rental Fund, the Capital Maintenance Fund, the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, the 2016 Capital Projects Fund, the Early Childhood Learning Center Capital Projects Fund and the Sinking Fund Capital Projects Fund. The item notes that the resolution does not have to be read in its entirety but must be made part of the official minutes. The resolution resolves that the general appropriations and budget of the Troy School District for fiscal year 2018-19 for those funds be amended and approved as attached and made part of the official minutes of the March 19, 2019 regular meeting; the Food Service Fund figure is 4,244,139.

**Personnel.** Item 6.A is a consideration of elementary and secondary personnel recommendations.

**Business 8.A: districtwide site work projects.** The resolution awards the bid for site work projects to Asphalt Specialists, Inc. in the amount of $822,140.00 as an expenditure of the Building and Site Sinking Fund, with a bid tabulation attached listing bid packages, companies and total costs for competing vendors.

**Business 8.B: districtwide asbestos abatement.** The resolution awards the bid for asbestos abatement to Trust Thermal Abatement in the amount of $288,420.00 as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund and the Building and Site Sinking Fund. The supporting material includes an asbestos abatement bid tabulation organized by bid number, buildings, contractor and bid amount, and a NOVA Environmental contractor award recommendation.

**Business 8.C: the 2019 School Building and Site Bonds.** The item records that the $125,000,000 bond issue was passed by the voters on November 5, 2013, that the district wishes to proceed with issuing the third series of bonds in an amount not to exceed $27,000,000, and that Dr. Richard Machesky and Rick West will be the individuals authorized to accept a purchase offer on the bonds. The resolution authorizes the issuance of bonds designated the "2019 School Building and Site Bonds" in an amount not to exceed $27,000,000, with the attached resolution in its entirety made a part of the official minutes of the March 19, 2019 regular meeting.

The attached authorizing resolution is captioned Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, Resolution Authorizing 2019 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation), and is framed for adoption at the regular meeting held March 19, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. local time. It recites that on November 5, 2013 the qualified electors of the School District approved a proposal authorizing the issuance of bonds in an aggregate amount of not to exceed $125,000,000, to be issued in one or more series, for the purpose of remodeling, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and re-furnishing school buildings and other facilities to enhance security and for other purposes; acquiring and installing technology equipment and technology infrastructure in school buildings and other facilities; constructing additions to school buildings; preparing, developing and improving sites at school buildings and other facilities; and the purchase of school buses — referred to as the 2013 Bond Proposal. It further recites that under the provisions of Section 6, Article IX and Section 16, Article IX of the Michigan Constitution of 1963, the tax levies for bonds authorized pursuant to the 2013 Bond Proposal shall be without limitation as to rate or amount, and that the bonds will be issued in one or more series based on the type of bonds issued, in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed the authorized figure.

**Business 8.D: preschool technology cabling.** The resolution awards the bid for cabling infrastructure for the Troy School District Preschool to Complete Interactive Technologies in the amount of $59,905.31 as an expenditure of the Early Childhood Center Fund, following an earlier bid update brought to the March 5 workshop.

**Business 8.E: aquatic sports timing equipment for Athens.** The final business item covers the purchase and installation of aquatic sports timing equipment for Athens High School.

The outcomes of these items are recorded in the March 19, 2019 minutes carried in the following month's packet: site work to Asphalt Specialists at $822,140.00 (resolution 19-029), asbestos abatement to Trust Thermal Abatement at $288,420.00 (19-030), the $27,000,000 bond authorization (19-031), preschool cabling to Complete Interactive Technologies at $59,905.31 (19-032) and aquatic sports timing equipment to Riegle Timing Consultants LLC at $65,008.00 (19-033), each adopted 7-0.
